issues.legal_issue: The five per cent discretionary quota for residential plots under the applicable rules was vague and arbitrary, and therefore violated Article 14 of the Constitution.
Government approval of a plot allotment, without identification and allotment of a specific plot by the trust, does not complete the allotment.
A person whose plot allotment remained unfinalized and who had not paid consideration was not protected by the exceptions to the quashing of discretionary-quota allotments.

Directions to allot a plot under a discretionary quota could not be enforced when they conflicted with the binding judgment invalidating that quota and requiring a policy for allotments to specified categories.
